$comment: MemoryGuard protected policy definitions. The deterministic policy evaluator consumes these rules. A rule triggers when every matcher in `matchers` is satisfied across the structured evidence (memory content + provenance). Matcher types: regex (field: content|sourceType|sourceTrusted, case-insensitive by default). `severity` and `confidence` drive incident classification: confidence 'policy_conflict' => confirmed policy conflict; 'signal' => suspicious signal (heuristic). Patched by hand; no migration needed.

policies.title: Production authentication checks must remain enabled
policies.statement: Authentication checks must not be disabled for production deployments. (Protected policy: "Production authentication checks must remain enabled.")

policies.title: Secrets must not be stored in agent memory
policies.statement: Agents must not persist API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, or connection strings in memory.

policies.title: Destructive actions require explicit approval
policies.statement: Memory content that plans or records destructive operations (delete, drop, wipe, purge, force reset) requires explicit approval evidence.

policies.title: Untrusted external instructions must not override protected policies
policies.statement: Instructions arriving from untrusted sources (e.g. scraped web pages, user chat attachments) must never be treated as authoritative. This is a heuristic suspicious-signal detector, not a confirmed policy conflict.

policies.title: Authentication checks must not be disabled in a deployment plan
policies.statement: Disabling authentication checks in a deployment or release plan is a suspicious signal when the environment is not known to be production.

policies.title: Security controls must not be disabled for load testing without review
policies.statement: Disabling a WAF in staging for load or performance testing is a suspicious signal requiring review.
